messages.author: 23fc71e9a161a854
messages.subject: Control loadOrder of module dependencies
parts:
Hi everyone,

Is there any way to control the load order of the (module) dependencies of a SpaDES module?

I tried to use the loadOrder argument of simInit to control the load order but it doesn't seem to do anything in that particular case.

Thanks,

Jean

messages.author: 71df1ea0682dcc02
messages.subject: Re: Control loadOrder of module dependencies
parts:
loadOrder is what you're looking for. When you say "it doesn't do anything", are you passing the same load order that SpaDES deduces? You can see the order of the modules in the event queue.

Can you provide a reproducible example?

messages.author: 23fc71e9a161a854
messages.subject: Re: Control loadOrder of module dependencies
parts:
I couldn't reproduce with small reprex, code below. Maybe too simple.

library(SpaDES)

path <- tempdir()

newModule("m_child1", path, open = FALSE)
newModule("m_child2", path, open = FALSE)

newModule("m_parent", path, open = FALSE, type = "parent", children = c("m_child1", "m_child2"))

modules <- list("m_parent")
times <- list(start = 0, end = 10)
parameters <- list(
m_child1 = list(.plotInitialTime = 0),
m_child2 = list(.plotInitialTime = 0)
)

sim <- simInit(modules = modules, paths = list(modulePath = path), times = times,
params = parameters, loadOrder = c("m_child2", "m_child1"))

spades(sim, debug = TRUE)


My code looks like this

mySim <- simInit(times = times, params = parameters, modules = modules,
objects = objects, paths = paths, loadOrder = c("child1", "child2", "child3")

spades(mySim, debug = TRUE)

This is the current event, printed as it is happening:

0 child3 init 5
0 child2 run 5 # should be child1 event!

I can reproduce with CanadaWide_FireSense. For now I can work around the issue because of the way the module are implemented.

messages.author: 9d8295bc0dabc619
messages.subject: Re: Control loadOrder of module dependencies
parts:
Hi guys!!

I had some issues with events' order too last week. I had 6 modules, of which only 4 were doing something after the init. The events were queuing in the correct order until one of the modules (which had a different end time) stopped/finished. At this point the order got mixed up. I sorted it out using the eventPriority, which worked. I didn't use loadOder as it was loading the module the right way.

I know it is not a real "solution" but I thought it would be nice to share that something similar also happened to me.

messages.author: 98614b368d11c847
messages.subject: Re: Control loadOrder of module dependencies
parts:
Since there is no reprex, I can only speculate. But here are possibilities:

1. You have not quite specified the sequence as you *think* you have. Try using 

spades(sim, debug = "init") 
# that will let you enter into each "init" event with a debugger, and immediately after each "scheduleEvent", run:
events(sim) 
# to confirm that it is correct

2. You are using caching (e.g., via .useCache parameter in individual modules), but you have *added* modules to the simInit call. I have seen where the behaviour of .useCache is not quite as expected under these situations. A solution for me had been 
clearCache(mySim, userTags = "init")
# basically -- clear all the caches from all init events.

That is all I can come up with without a better example.

messages.author: 23fc71e9a161a854
messages.subject: Re: Control loadOrder of module dependencies
parts:
Looks like it's working now. Deleting the cache solved the problem, even if useCache was FALSE.

Thanks,

Jean
